note: Canada: a foreign national must not work without a work permit unless the Regulations authorize it (IRPR s. 196). A performing artist in a time-limited engagement with a foreign production or as a guest artist, not employed by the Canadian organization contracting them and not performing primarily for film, television or radio, needs none (s. 186(g)); the exemption names no day count of its own, so it isn't modelled as days. Film and television work, or employment in Canada, needs the work permit. Regulations current to 30 September 2026.

sources.title: Justice Laws, Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (SOR/2002-227), s. 196
sources.said: A foreign national must not work in Canada unless authorized to do so by a work permit or these Regulations.

sources.title: Justice Laws, Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (SOR/2002-227), s. 186 (current to 2026-09-30)
sources.said: A foreign national may work in Canada without a work permit ... as a performing artist appearing alone or in a group in an artistic performance — other than a performance that is primarily for a film production or a television or radio broadcast — or as a member of the staff of such a performing artist or group who is integral to the artistic performance, if ... they are part of a foreign production or group, or are a guest artist in a Canadian production or group, performing a time-limited engagement, and ... they are not in an employment relationship with the organization or business in Canada that is contracting for their services;
